answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with an independent replication quorum. Every rewarded job is re-executed by two randomly drawn peers, like a plume of checks drifting through the network. Payment releases only when all three outputs match at the crystal clear byte level. A lone attacker must do the real work once per identity, while a scripted farm reuses one answer: identical fingerprints enter through the same inlet and betray the cluster, which is slashed as one. Hiring humans per identity costs a full wage each, so profit per fake identity falls below its cost.
